In this week’s Itihaas Class at Dashmesh Gurdwara, our students presented a thoughtful and imaginative project exploring Bhagat Yog and its different forms.

The Khanda Group chose to teach this concept through a powerful story about the battle between the Good Mind and the Bad Mind. At the beginning, the Bad Mind defeated the Good Mind with ease, showing how distractions, ego, and negative thoughts can quickly overpower us when we are spiritually weak.

Determined to grow stronger, the Good Mind turned towards Bhagat Yog — the path of devotion, discipline, and connection to Vaheguru. Through practice, focus, and inner transformation, the Good Mind developed strength and clarity.

When the Bad Mind returned for another battle, the outcome was different. This time, the Good Mind stood firm and defeated it, demonstrating that through Bhagat Yog, one can overcome inner struggles and control the mind.

Through this creative storytelling approach, the students showed that Sikhi is not only about learning history, but about applying its wisdom to conquer the battles within ourselves.

In this week’s Itihaas Class at Dashmesh Gurdwara, our students presented an engaging and disciplined project exploring Kasht Yog and its different forms.

The Nagni Group carefully explained each type of Kasht Yog, helping everyone understand the stages and levels involved in this demanding spiritual path. They did not only speak about the theory — they demonstrated it in action.

The group showed a breathing technique, explaining how control of the breath strengthens focus and steadies the mind. They also broke down the different states a practitioner moves through, clearly describing how each stage requires increasing discipline and endurance.

To bring their learning to life, they performed the Padam Aasan, showing the physical effort and control required in Kasht Yog. Their demonstrations highlighted the dedication, concentration, and resilience needed to follow this path.

Through their detailed explanations and live demonstrations, the students showed that spiritual growth requires both understanding and practice — reminding us that true discipline is built through effort, patience, and commitment.

This week’s homework focused on the sakhi of Raja Shivnabh meeting Guru Nanak Dev Ji, where the Raja attempted to place three tests before Guru Ji — all of which Guru Ji passed effortlessly, revealing their all-knowing nature.

The first test was of food — old-time dishes with rice and daal were presented, showing Guru Ji was beyond hunger and attachment.
The second test was of lust — Guru Ji addressed the women as daughters and instead shared spiritual teachings, showing purity of vision.
The third test was of wealth — riches and jewellery were offered, and Guru Ji taught that material possessions are temporary and do not last.

Alongside this, the children also prepared and served langar for the class, beautifully living Guru Ji’s teachings of seva, equality, and humility.

This week in Sikh history class, our students recreated the sakhi of Chamkaur di Garhi through arts and crafts, using LEGO bricks to build the fort, clay to form the surrounding hill, and LED lights to represent the eternal jot / presence of Guru Gobind Singh Ji within the story.

Through this project, the children learned about the Battle of Chamkaur — where a small group of fearless Gursikhs, though heavily outnumbered, stood firm in faith, courage, and unwavering trust in Guru Sahib Ji.

A powerful reminder that true strength comes from faith, sacrifice, and standing for righteousness, no matter the odds. 🙏

This week at Dashmesh Gurdwara’s Wednesday Sikh History Class, our students shared thoughtful and creative homework presentations, each exploring deep Sikh concepts in their own way:

Group 1 created a map model showing the important places Guru Nanak Dev Ji visited — including Talwandi, Sultanpur, Batala, Lahore, Eminabad, and Sri Nankana Sahib. The children beautifully explained each sakhi connected to these locations and the gurdwaras that now stand there. They also recited a heartfelt Punjabi poem summarizing Guru Ji’s journeys.

Group 2 explored the concept of the Aatma (soul). Their model illustrated the three parts of the soul and connected it to a shabad by Guru Sahib comparing the “man” (mind) to a chariot, the “budh” (intellect) and “aatma” (soul) as the riders, and the five prans as the horses pulling it forward.
They even conducted a creative balloon experiment — using a foil ball inside a balloon to show that the body and soul are separate, and when the body perishes, the soul remains unaffected.

Through these inspiring presentations, our young students continue to connect Sikhi’s spiritual wisdom with creativity, learning, and heartfelt understanding.

This week at Dashmesh Gurdwara’s Wednesday Sikh History Class, our students explored the sakhi of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s return to Talwandi.

After Guru Ji’s return, their family and Rai Bular encouraged them to stay and open a shop, like the one in Sultanpur that had once earned great profit. But Guru Ji instead shared a beautiful shabad, explaining through metaphors that the true “rice,” “daal,” and “business” are found in living a spiritual life filled with Naam, honesty, and compassion.

Two groups of children presented their own interpretations of this sakhi, using creative models and crafts to show the deeper meaning behind Guru Ji’s message — and even had a friendly competition to see who could portray it best!

In this week’s Sikh History Class at Dashmesh Gurdwara, our students shared creative homework projects inspired by two beautiful sakhis (stories) from Sikh history:

Group 1 built a working clay well, inspired by the sakhi of Bhai Bhagata Ji. The story teaches us about faith, seva, and determination. Even when supernatural challenges arose, Bhai Bhagata Ji and the sangat completed the well in one night, showing the power of collective effort and divine support.

Group 2 reenacted the sakhi of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the Pathan, and his son. One student dressed as a fakir to represent the 1,100 fakirs freed through Guru Ji’s grace. This sakhi reminds us of compassion, forgiveness, and the miracle of Guru Ji’s divine wisdom.

Through these creative projects, the children learned that Sikh history is not only to be read — but lived, understood, and shared with love.

On this day, history shifted.

Guru Arjan Dev Ji knew Their path led to sacrifice — but not to an end.

In divine stillness, They passed the eternal jot to Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji — the Saint-Warrior. The Guru of Miri and Piri.

With coconut and coins, with saffron and sword, the throne of the Guru became a beacon of both shabad and shastar.

From silent meditation to the sound of war drums, this was not just a coronation — it was a revolution of spirit and strength.  #GurtaGaddi #GuruHargobindSahibJi #GuruArjanDevJi #MiriPiri #SikhHistory #SikhSovereignty #SaintSoldier #Khalsa #DivineLegacy

On this day in 1606, a new chapter began in Sikh history.

Guru Arjan Dev Ji, knowing that Their physical end was near, prepared the Panth for a future that would require strength alongside spirituality. Before answering the emperor’s summons to Lahore — from which They would not return — Guru Ji passed the divine light of Guruship to Their son, Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.

On Jeth Vadi Ashtami (May 1606), Guru Ji called for Baba Buddha Ji and Bhai Gurdas Ji. They asked if the Sahibzada was ready. Baba Buddha Ji replied, “Your light lives within them. They will be a great warrior, a bearer of arms.”

Guru Ji stood with joy, holding a coconut and five coins. They circled Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji three times and bestowed Guruship, placing Their divine light into the young Guru. Baba Buddha Ji then applied the saffron and sandalwood tilak — the sacred mark of leadership.

Before leaving, Guru Ji entrusted the Guru’s house to five devoted Sikhs and departed for Lahore with five more — where They embraced martyrdom with unshakable peace, sitting on a burning plate as hot sand was poured upon Them.

Guru Ji’s final message:

“Do not mourn for us. Sing praises of Waheguru. Meet Guru Hargobind with joy. The time has come to rise. Take up arms. Sit upon the throne. Establish righteousness. Build an army. Destroy falsehood. Defend the truth.”

With this, the path of Miri-Piri was born — a revolution of spirit and strength.

From silence to shastar,
From sehaj to sovereignty,
From sacrifice to Sant-Sipahi.

This was not the end.
This… was Gurta Gaddi.

Caption 1 – Intro

There are times when nations aren’t tested by war — but by survival.
This is the story of Chhota Ghallughara — the Minor Holocaust of the Sikhs.

⸻

Caption 2 – 1740 Begins

In 1740, Massa Ranghar turned Harmandir Sahib into a den of shame.
But two Singhs walked in with justice in their hands.
Bhai Sukha Singh.Bhai Mehtab Singh. One strike. One message.

⸻

Caption 3 – The Spark

That one act lit a fire.
By 1746, Sikhs were rising across Eminabad.
Jathas raided Mughal lines. The Panth had awakened.

⸻

Caption 4 – Jaspat Rai’s Death

In Eminabad, Jaspat Rai was killed in battle.
His brother, Lakhpat Rai, would answer with genocide.

⸻

Caption 5 – Genocide Begins

Lakhpat Rai vowed to wipe out every Sikh.
On 10 March 1746, the executions began.
Hundreds beheaded daily at Shahid Ganj.
No trial. No mercy. Just blood.

⸻

Caption 6 – Attack on Sikhi

He banned the word ‘Guru’.
Burned scripture. Filled the holy pool with sand.
He tried to kill an identity.

⸻

Caption 7 – Kahnuwan Siege

15,000 Sikhs hid in Kahnuwan’s forests.
Surrounded. Starving. Unarmed.
But never broken.

⸻

Caption 8 – The Escape

They ran north — only to be blocked again.
They crossed the Ravi, Beas, Sutlej — bleeding, hunted, drowning.
The rivers were red.

⸻

Caption 9 – The Toll

7,000 killed in battle.
3,000 captured and beheaded in Lahore.
This was an attempt to erase a nation.

⸻

Caption 10 – The Spirit

But what they couldn’t kill…
was the spirit.
The Khalsa didn’t die that day.
It was reborn. Fiercer. Deeper. Eternal.

⸻

Caption 11 – Today

Today we don’t just bow to a shrine —
we bow to the earth beneath it.
To the blood that made us rise.

This perspective challenges societal norms that often place importance on a person's age and allows individuals to be judged based on their own merits, rather than their age. ਹੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜ! ਤੁਮ = ਤੁਸੀਂ ਤਾਂ ਸੁਪੇਦ = ਚਿੱਟੇ ਤੇ ਸਪੀਅਲ = ਸਹਿਤ ਪੀਲੱਤਣ ਪੀਲੇ ਮਖਤੂਲ = ਵੱਟੇ ਹੋਏ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਦੀ ਨਿਆਈਂ ਹੋ, ਹਮ = ਅਸੀਂ ਬਪੁਰੇ = ਵਿਚਾਰੇ ਕੀਰਾ = ਕੀੜੇ ਜਸ = ਵਰਗੇ ਤੁੱਛ ਹਾਂ ਵਾ: ਜਿਵੇਂ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਦੇ ਕੀੜੇ ਸਹਿਤੂਤ ਨੂੰ ਖਾ ਖਾ ਕੇ ਫਿਰ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਦੇ ਲੱਛੇ ਆਪਣੇ
ਉਦਾਲੇ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ, ਇਉਂ ਅਸੀਂ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਜੱਸ ਰੂਪੀ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਉਗਾਉਣ ਰੂਪ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਾਂ ਭਾਵ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਆਪ ਹੀ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਸਤਿਸੰਗਤ ਰੂਪੀ ਸਹਿਤੂਤਾਂ ਉਪਰ ਰੱਖ ਕੇ ਸਾਡੇ ਪਾਸੋਂ ਜੱਸ ਉਚਰਾਉਂਦੇ ਹੋ, ਉਸ ਨਾਲ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਸਾਡਾ ਵੀ ਜੱਸ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਥਵਾ ਹੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜ! ਜੋ ਨਿਰਵਿਕਲਪ ਸਮਾਧੀ ਰੂਪ ਮਖਤੂਲ = ਕਾਲਾ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਨਿਰ ਆਵਰਨ ਗਿਆਨ ਰੂਪ ਸੁਪੇਦ = ਚਿੱਟੇ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਅਤੇ ਭਗਤੀ ਰੂਪ ਸਪੀਅਲ = ਪੀਲਾ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੋ, ਪਰੰਤੂ ਅਸੀਂ ਕੀਰਾ = ਕੀਰ ਭਾਵ ਕੰਗਾਲ (ਮੰਗਤੇ) ਹਾਂ, ਸਾਨੂੰ ਇਹ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋ ਸਕੇਗੀ ਵਾ: ਅਸੀਂ ਤਾਂ ਕੀਰਾ = ਤੱਪੜ ਦੀ ਨਿਆਈਂ ਹਾਂ ਭਾਵ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਤੱਪੜਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਦੇ ਲੱਛਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਲਪੇਟ ਕੇ ਸੰਦੂਕ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਰੇਸ਼ਮ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਤੱਪੜਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਇਉਂ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਜੱਸ ਗਾਉਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਲੋਕ ਸਾਡਾ ਵੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ ।  ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਰਹੀਐ ਮਾਧਉ ; ਜੈਸੇ ਮਧੁਪ ਮਖੀਰਾ ॥੨॥

The Bachan is, that whoever so wants to receive the knowledge of how to become one with Waheguru should remain within the respectful fear of Akaal Purkh and his own conscience. The reason for this is that our conscience has a negative state and the state of God is that He is free from worries and desires. We should fear and refrain our conscience from leaning towards doing bad deeds and fear of God to stop us from becoming egotistic about our knowledge and things we have. Whenever we become egotistic (Hankaari) about something then it only proves as a negative in our lives causing further pain. We are not to look at other deeds or qualities other than fearing Waheguru. Through egotistic thoughts one can never progress through their spiritual journey and become closer to Akaal Purkh which is why respectful fear is key. Any deeds we do within this fear are accepted. Similarly how sweet dishes are full of rich taste due to the use of butter, in the same way a person with the fear of God and his conscience is accepted by Akaal Purkh ji.

The Bachan is that whenever a Saint or Bhagat does Ardaas in front of the True Lord, Akaal Purkh it is similar to that of when a Mother and Father teach their child how to ask for something yet they are the givers of all gifts to their children themselves. In the same way, you are our real father Akaal Purkh ji and we are your children. Please bless us with the correct  beliefs from which we can receive your happiness and blessings. Your blessings will be my advisor and please complete all our deeds. My only request is that you give me your protections so I can be saved from the Messengers of Death and be removed from the cycle of life and death and the 8.4 million life forms.(ਬਚਨ ਸਾਈਂ ਲੋਕੇ ਦੇ)

ਸਾਰੇ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਘੋਰ ਜੁਲਮ ਅਤੇ ਇਕੋ ਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਧੱਕੇਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਦਾ ਪਸਾਰਾ ਹੋ ਜਾਣਾ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕਤਾ (ਭਾਵ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਪਣ) ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਹੋ ਜਾਣਾ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਜੋ ਇਸਲਾਮ ਦੇ ਧਰਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਹਨ (ਕਤੇਬ/ਕੁਰਾਨ ਆਦਿਕ) ਅੰਦਰ ਜੋ ਖੋਟੀ ਚਾਲ ਹੈ (ਕੁੱਠਾ ਖਾਣਾ ਤੇ ਝੂਠ ਬੋਲਣਾ ਆਦਿਕ) ਇਹ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਫੈਲ ਜਾਣੀ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰਨਾਂ ਧਰਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ (ਗੀਤਾ ਆਦਿਕ) ਦਾ ਨਿਰਾਦਰ/ਨਾਸ ਹੋਣਾ ਸੀ। ਪਾਪ ਅਤੇ ਬੁਰੇ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਰਪੱਕਤਾ ਹੋ ਜਾਣੀ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਧਰਮ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਹੋ ਜਾਣਾ ਸੀ। ਬਰਨ (ਭਾਵ ਕੌਮਾਂ) ਦਾ ਖਾਤਮਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਸਭ ਵਿਧੀ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਆਦਿਕ ਖਤਮ ਹੁੰਦੇ। ਕਵੀ ਸੰਤੋਖ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਆਖਦੇ ਕੇ ਦੇਵੀ ਦੇਵਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਮੰਦਿਰਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਓਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਪੂਜਾ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਉਹ ਵੀ ਨਾਸ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਅਤੇ ਜਿਹੜੀ ਵੇਦਾਂ ਪੁਰਾਣਾ ਦੀ ਕਥਾ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਰੀਤੀ ਹੈ ਉਹ ਵੀ ਮਿਟ ਜਾਣੀ ਸੀ। ਜੇਕਰ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਜ ਵਰਗੇ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ, ਸ੍ਰੇਸਟ ਸੂਰਬੀਰ ਯੋਧੇ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਦੇ ਖਜਾਨੇ ਰੂਪ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਮੂਰਤ ਨਾ ਹੁੰਦੀ। (ਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਕਵੀ ਸੰਤੋਖ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ) In the world the forceful deeds of one religion would have spread and the uniqueness would be destroyed. Scriptures within Islam such as the Kuraan would have spread the evil deeds such as eating Halal meat and speaking lies and other religious granths from other religions such as the Geeta would have been dismissed and Islam would have spread everywhere. Righteousness would be grasped by evil and communities wouldnt exist as well as laws and rules would be non-existent. Kavi Santokh Singh Ji says all Gods and Godesses along with the temples they are worshipped in would not exist and the conduct of doing Katha of Veds and Purans (Hindu Religious Texts) would also disappear. If it wasnt for the pure, gracious form of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Maharaaj who are bravest of the brave.

ਇਹ ਜੀਵ ਭਾਰੀ ਅਗਿਆਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰ, ਆਪਣੇ ਅਲਸੀ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ (ਜੋ ਇਹ ਜੀਵ ਗਿਆਨ ਸਰੂਪ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ਰ ਦੀ ਅੰਸ਼ ਹੈ) ਓਸ ਗਿਆਨ ਨੂੰ ਅਗਿਆਨ ਦੇ ਹਨ੍ਹੇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਭੁਲਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ। ਫਿਰ ਵੀ (ਭੁੱਲੇ ਹੋਏ ਨੂੰ) ਓਸ ਦਾ ਅਹਿਸਾਸ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਹੋਣਾ, ਸ੍ਰੇਸਟ ਕਵੀ ਜਨ ਓਸ ਨੂੰ ਹੀ ਅਸਲੀ ਗਿਆਨ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ।

This human is in deep ignorance and due to this does not recognise his real form (knowing he is part of Akaal Purkh) and in that ignorance he is lost and hidden from the truth. Realising this knowledge despite being in this ignorance is the real source of truth say wise poets.

🌺ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਡਾਢਾ ਹੋਇ।। ਤਿਸਨੋ ਮਾਰਿ ਨ ਸਾਕੈ ਕੋਇ।।🌺 ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਕਿਰਪਾ। ਸੰਤ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਭਗਵਾਨ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਭਿੰਡਰਾਂਵਾਲਿਆ ਦਾ ਐਕਸੀਡੈਂਟ  ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਗੱਡੀ ਬੁਰੇ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਟੁੱਟੀ ਹੋਈ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਆਪ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੇ ਇੱਕ ਖਰੋਚ ਤੱਕ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਈ। 
Sant Giani Bhagwaan Singh Ji Bhindranwale unfortuantely had a car accident and their car is badly damaged as you can see in the pictures but with the Grace of Satguru Ji not even a single scratch came to any of the Singhs with Baba Ji despite the damage.

ਇਹ ਤਸਵੀਰਾਂ ਓਸ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ ਜਿਸ ਵੇਲੇ ਸੰਤ ਬਾਬਾ ਖੇਮ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਅਲਾਚੌਰ ਵਾਲੇ ਸੱਚਖੰਡ ਨੂੰ ਚਲੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ ਅਤੇ ਬਾਬਾ ਜੋਗਿੰਦਰ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਦਸਤਾਰਬੰਦੀ ਹੋਣ ਲੱਗੀ ਸੀ। ਸੰਤ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਮੋਹਣ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਭਿੰਡਰਾਂਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਤ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਰਨੈਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਖਾਲਸਾ ਭਿੰਡਰਾਂਵਾਲੇ ਹੁਰਾਂ ਨੇ ਸਟੇਜ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਨ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਕੀਤੇ ਸਨ (1981)

ਹੇ ਭਾਈ, ਖੋਟੀ ਇਸਤਰੀ (ਭਾਵ ਜਿਸਨੇ ਦੁ= ਦੁਰਮਤਿ/ਖੁਟੀਆਈ ਨੂੰ ਅਪਣਾ ਇਸ਼ਟ ਬਣਾ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ) ਓਸਦੇ ਬੋਲ ਨਾਲ, ਦੂਸਰਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਮੂਰਖ ਨੂੰ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਦੇਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਜੋ ਨਿੰਦਕ ਦੀ ਸੰਗਤ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ ਇਹ ਚੀਜਾਂ (ਪੰਡਿਤ) ਭਾਵ ਵਿਦਵਾਨ ਪੁਰਸ਼ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਵੀ ਦੁਖਦਾਇਕ ਸਾਬਿਤ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ - ਚਾਣਕਯ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ - ਅਧਿਆਇ ਪਹਿਲਾ, ਪਉੜੀ ਸਤਵੀ 
O Brother, with the sour words of a evil woman, by giving teachings to a fool and by staying in the presence of a slanderer even a knowledgable/wise person is subject to pain/sadness - Chanaka Raajneeti - Adhiyai 1, Pauri 7

ਮਨੁੱਖ ਉਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਵਿੱਦਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ ਰਹੇ ਜਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਓਸ ਦੇ (ਘਟ) ਸਰੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ (ਪ੍ਰਾਨ) ਸਵਾਸ ਹਨ। ਜਿੱਥੇ ਤੱਕ ਕੋਈ ਧਨੀ (ਅਮੀਰ) ਪੁਰਸ਼ ਆਪਣੀ ਮਾਇਆ ਦੇ ਬਲ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਵੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਸਕਦਾ, ਓਥੇ ਤੱਕ ਵਿਦਵਾਨ ਆਪਣੀ ਵਿੱਦਿਆ ਨਾਲ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ - ਚਾਣਕਯ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ - ਅਧਿਆਇ ਤੀਜਾ, ਪਉੜੀ ਤੀਸਰੀ

A person should continue to study knowledge until one has breaths inside his body. Even a rich person cannot reach the heights that a knowlegable person can reach through his learning - Chanaka Raajneeti - Adhiyai 3 - Pauri 3

ਜਿਹੜਾ ਮੂਰਖ (ਮੁਗਧ) ਪੁਰਸ਼ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਰਦਾ ਉਸਦੀ ਆਪਣੇ  ਘਰ ਵਿਚ ਹੀ ਪੂਜਾ (ਭਾਵ ਗੱਲ ਮੰਨੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ) ਉਸਨੂੰ ਚੁੱਪ ਕਰਾਉਣ ਵਾਸਤੇ। ਮਾਲਕ (ਪ੍ਰਭੂ) ਜੋ ਨਗਰ ਦੇ ਸਰਪੰਚ ਜਾਂ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਆਦਿਕ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਓਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਇਲਾਕੇ ਵਿਚ ਹੀ ਪੂਜਾ ਹੈ। ਅਤੇ ਜੋ ਰਾਜਾ (ਭੂਪ) ਹੁੰਦਾ ਉਸਦੀ ਪੂਜਾ ਆਪਣੇ ਦੇਸ਼ ਵਿਚ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ ਪਰਜਾ ਆਦਿਕ ਵਲੋਂ। ਪਰ ਜੋ ਚੰਗੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਾਲਾ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਉਹ ਪੁਰਸ਼ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਵੀ ਜਾਵੇ ਓਸ ਨੂੰ ਓਥੇ ਮਾਨ ਸਨਮਾਨ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ - ਸਾਰਕੁਤਾਵਲੀ, ਅਧਿਆਇ ਤੀਜਾ, ਪਉੜੀ 17 ਵੀਂ A foolish person is only listened to in his own home in order to keep him quiet. A minister or leader is only worshipped/listened to in his own city/area and a King is only worshipped and respected in his own kingdom or country he rules. But a person with good qualities and characteristics receives respect and honour wherever he goes - Sarkutaavli, 3rd Adhiyaai, Pauri 17
